open_questions: Gaia RUWE 15.95 and excess_noise_sig 2159 indicate the M dwarf host may itself be a close unresolved binary; radial-velocity monitoring needed to test for stellar-mass companion and to rule out diluted EB despite flat bottom.

Sector depth change 9686±1763 ppm vs 15098±1241 ppm (p_constant 0.01208, depth_change_pct 43.67) and transit_depths p_consistent 0.008621173042045328 with share_of_top_3 0.975 from only 4 transits; multi-colour transit photometry or additional sectors needed to confirm depth stability and rule out spot-crossings on active star.

Duration ratio 1.541 (observed_h 3 vs central_h 1.947) exceeds 1.5 and fit_b 0.8214 with star_density_penalty 111 on very short-period 12.8 d orbit; stellar-density mismatch deserves follow-up to confirm circular, planet-consistent density vs eccentric blended binary
dossier.public_summary: A 3.8 Earth-radius dip repeats every 12.8 days with a flat bottom, no sign of a second eclipse, and no nearby star in the same TESS pixel able to mimic it. The host is an active 0.30 Rsun M dwarf; depth changes modestly between two sectors and between the four transits, which is common for a spotted, low-S/N signal. The small size and transit shape make a planet the best explanation, with stellar activity and the star's own astrometric binary signs as the main remaining uncertainties.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed (negative V) transit shape favours a transiting planet over grazing or stellar eclipsing binary; V of -3.921 is well below 0 threshold for V-shaped.
Planet-sized undiluted radius 3.8 Rearth from undiluted_depth_ppm 13420 and rp_over_rstar 0.1158, well below stellar regime, supports planet even accounting for high RUWE star.
No significant odd/even difference and no secondary dip at phase 0.4251 (SNR 1.965 vs depth_ppm 13380) with no signal at phase 0.5, arguing against binary at twice period on target.

Star does vary (amplitude_ppm 18626 ppm in sector 55) but signal_over_rotation is null at 12.7704 d; dip period is not a multiple of a detected rotation period with low false alarm, and phase_curve chi2 15.23 on 9 dof with ratio_to_depth 0.09663 shows no large out-of-eclipse swing.

No star within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can produce the 13380 ppm dip with <=25% eclipse (could_cause_within_1px 0), so neighbour eclipse is not plausible; closest that could is 34.9 arcsec requiring 0.284 eclipse, farther than TESS pixel, and centroid is inconclusive only because no sector with a clear difference image.
